title: every-datarecorder-declares-when-it-was-started-last-read-and-how-often-it-expects-reading
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> [TICKETME:waiting] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(declared-cadence-discriminates) -> PROVED
intention: Every datarecorder carries when it started, when it was last read, how often it expects to be read, and whether it drains or reports-and-holds — so an unread recorder raises a trouble by itself instead of waiting to be noticed.
why: A datarecorder nobody reads accumulates silently — the same shape as the inspector findings that 'accumulated silently' until today. Akien 2026-09-04: with started/lastread/expected_read_frequency on every recorder, 'we can also automatically issue trouble tickets on unread data recorders.' The lived symptom is data written for a reader who never comes, discovered by accident.
how: SETTLED AT THE CAST 2026-09-07 (the 'names are Akien's' reason is retired by his ruling that nothing before PROVEME waits at his gate). A `reading.json` berths beside `records.jsonl` inside the recorder's own directory at ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/data_recorder/<name>/ — the holder's instance home, which is where Law 6 already puts a tool's ongoing state, so the holder owns and gates it and the tool gates nothing of its own. Four fields: `started` (ISO, written by the recorder on its FIRST write() — not on construction, because BaseDevice mints a recorder for every device on every boot and a construction stamp would silently mean 'last booted'), `last_read` (ISO or null), `expected_read_frequency_seconds` (int or null), `on_read` ('drain' | 'hold'). A reader stamps through one new door, DataRecorder.stamp_read(ids=None), which moves last_read and — when on_read is 'drain' and ids were given — calls the existing clear(ids) in the same act, so a reader cannot stamp without draining or drain without stamping. Declaration comes from the DEVICE: DataRecorder.__init__ takes the two optional settings and BaseDevice passes through what the device declares. UNDECLARED IS RED, NOT DEFAULT (Law 9) — there is no fallback frequency, because a fallback would silently green the recorders that have no reader at all, and that is the hollow build (Law 8). A new at-rest probe on the existing probe surface (NOT new ground-loop work) globs the recorders through cairn.tools.base.address, never a hand-spelled path, and raises via DiagnosticBase.raise_trouble — no import of the trouble device and no bus (ticket 9579a6f9cec6). TWO DISTINCT IDENTITIES, deliberately not folded: 'recorder-declares-no-reader-<device>-<instance>-<name>' and 'recorder-read-overdue-<device>-<instance>-<name>'. Merging them would tell the reader that 'nobody ever specified this' and 'somebody specified it and missed' are the same defect, and they are opposite instructions.
falsifier: DONE when a recorder deliberately left unread past its declared frequency raises a trouble on the next beat, and a recorder read on time does not — both halves, because the half that only fires is a check that cannot fail. THIRD TOOTH added at the cast: a recorder declaring nothing raises its own distinct identity ('declares no reader'), separate from 'read is overdue'. WRONG INTENT if most recorders have no meaningful reader cadence — then the switch (drain vs hold) is the whole feature and the frequency is noise. NOTE, measured: with 10/10 recorders unread today the frequency's DISCRIMINATING power is untestable until readers exist, which is exactly what the WATCHME below watches for.
traces_to: Law 7 — an unread record is a silent error; Law 3 — 'expected read frequency' makes the claim that something is read measurable. Law 10 — the recorder can measure its own reading.

watchme.trigger: On each at-rest beat, after the overdue check runs: record the population — how many recorders declare a frequency, how many declare none, how many have a non-null last_read, and the spread of declared frequencies. It fires on the beat because the data is already in hand; it costs one extra dict.
watchme.enough: Enough when at least three recorders have a non-null last_read (real readers exist) AND the declared frequencies have taken at least two distinct values. Then the question is answered either way: if the overdue troubles discriminate — some recorders green, some red — the frequency is load-bearing and the watch closes green; if every reader reads on every beat or every declaration collapses to one value, the WRONG INTENT clause is confirmed, the drain/hold switch was the whole feature, and the watch closes by kicking a ticket to strip the frequency. Deliberately NOT time-bounded: with 10/10 recorders unread, a clock would only measure how long readers take to appear, which is a different question.
watchme.carrier: A verdict artifact against this ticket's WRONG INTENT clause, written by the probe on the beat it reaches `enough`, carrying the population counts and the distinct-frequency set as its evidence rather than a summary of them.
watchme.nexus: The data_recorder tool's own charter tree at cairn/tools/data_recorder/ — the verdict amends the charter's account of what a recorder is FOR (a mailbox with a reader, or a mailbox that holds), which is the claim the census already put in doubt.
watchme.consumer: CC, through the operator inbox — the same surface the overdue troubles land on, so the answer arrives where the question is already visible.

owner: cairn device owns folder-based datarecorders (press_office is one). The field names and the drain/hold switch were settled at the cast, 2026-09-07, under Akien's ruling that nothing before PROVEME waits at his gate.
author: CC
cast_under: Akien 2026-09-07 (idea 811780d76281): 'the goal before we let go of fable is to move everything that doesn't have the word cognition in it to BUILDME'
measured_at_cast: CENSUS 2026-09-07, and it is the finding this ticket now stands on: 10 records.jsonl on disk holding 1,817 records — harbor_master 1429, librarian 156, codemother 59, charter 46, press_office 40, cairn 32, tester 31, disk_only 12, test_no_verb_device 9, inference_domain 3. Exactly 2 construction sites (cairn/tools/base/device.py:240, cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/discovered.py:103) and ZERO readers: nothing in the corpus calls .read() or .clear() on a recorder outside that recorder's own proofs. Every one is BaseDevice.receive()'s default sink for verbless mail — mail arrives, is recorded 'for later evaluation', and nothing evaluates. This CONFIRMS the why rather than killing the ticket ('data written for a reader who never comes, discovered by accident'), and it prices the design: undeclared-is-red fires on all ten the first beat after this lands, which under the trouble damper is ten tickets at count 1 — the improvement backlog doing its job, not a flood.

gates_bound.proved_by: cairn/tools/data_recorder/proofs/test_reading_declaration.py, sealed through TesterDevice.run_proof. Teeth: (1) overdue raises on a frozen clock; (2) inside-frequency raises NOTHING; (3) undeclared raises a DIFFERENT identity; (4) stamp_read drains-and-stamps under 'drain', stamps only under 'hold'; (5) `started` is written on first write(), not on construction. Teeth 2 and 5 fail if the feature is stubbed green (Law 8).
gates_bound.feeds_back_to_origin_on_failure: A red at PROVEME kicks back to BUILDME through cairn.tools.base.transitions.emit; the probe's own troubles are the standing operational feedback and land in the operator inbox on the beat.
gates_bound.at_rest_probe_gate: the WATCHME emission gate resolves ARMED from the probe berth; the probe must exist on disk before PROVEME -> WATCHME crosses.
gates_bound.check_type: deterministic — a clock comparison and a file read, no LLM in the fire path.

children: none, because this is a leaf: one tool file, one pass-through in cairn/tools/base/device.py, one probe, one proof. The three teeth are teeth in one proof, not separable nodes — tooth 2 is only meaningful beside tooth 1. The reader that would eventually call stamp_read is NOT a child and must not become one: this ticket measures the absence of reading, and building its own consumer would green its own measurement.

decisions.text: reading.json is written by DataRecorder._write_reading beside records.jsonl with exactly four keys (started, last_read, expected_read_frequency_seconds, on_read); write(record, *, now=None) calls it after the append with first_write=True so started is stamped once, on the first write, and never moved; construction touches no disk and reading() returns None until the first write; the settings are ALWAYS the constructor's, so a holder that changes its declaration is read as it now declares.
decisions.step: unlisted: the recorder's self-declaration (reading.json, started, last_read, expected_read_frequency_seconds, on_read, stamp_read door)

decisions.text: stamp_read(ids=None, *, now=None) -> int: under on_read 'drain' with ids it calls clear(ids) and then stamps last_read=now in the same act; under 'hold' or with no ids it stamps only; returns the count cleared. __init__(base_dir, *, expected_read_frequency_seconds=None, on_read=None) refuses with ValueError an on_read outside ('drain','hold') or a frequency that is not a positive int (bool excluded).
decisions.step: unlisted: DataRecorder gains reading.json (started on first write, last_read, expected_read_frequency_seconds, on_read) and stamp_read(ids=None)

decisions.text: The declaration is two CLASS ATTRIBUTES on the holder — RECORDER_READ_FREQUENCY_SECONDS: int|None = None and RECORDER_ON_READ: str|None = None — declared on BaseDevice (cairn/tools/base/device.py) and on _FeedbackDevice (ground_loop/discovered.py); a device class overrides them to declare; _get_recorder at both sites passes them through as DataRecorder(path, expected_read_frequency_seconds=..., on_read=...). None is the honest undeclared state and reads red under the probe; no default is invented anywhere.
decisions.step: unlisted: the holders pass through what the device declares (two settings: expected_read_frequency_seconds and on_read)

decisions.text: A probe module raises through ModuleRaiser('data_recorder', roots=roots) — the DiagnosticBase surface for a module (cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py) — never by importing the trouble device and never over the bus; the raise sits in the probe's TRIGGER, memoized per beat via probe.once(context, 'recorder_reading', ...), so a standing overdue raises every beat and the trouble drain folds recurrences on identity; the same pass calls raiser.reconcile_troubles('recorder-', <sorted identities observed>, by='cc', what_changed=...) so a recorder that gets read clears. Emissions land under instance/logs/data_recorder/0/ (measured) and the trouble shim drains that home like any device's.
decisions.step: unlisted: cairn/tools/data_recorder/probes/reading_is_declared_and_current.py globs held recorders, reads reading.json against clock, raises two distinct identities via DiagnosticBase.raise_trouble

decisions.text: The census is the pure function census(now, *, roots=None): recorders are found through address.held_tool_paths('data_recorder', roots) one level down (each child dir carrying reading.json or records.jsonl; name = the child dir name; device and instance read from the held path's parents). reading.json absent OR expected_read_frequency_seconds null -> recorder-declares-no-reader-<device>-<instance>-<name>; else since = last_read or started and (now - since) > frequency -> recorder-read-overdue-<device>-<instance>-<name>; otherwise the recorder is current. report(now, *, roots=None, raiser=None) raises and reconciles; the Probe declares to='harbor_master', body {nexus: hypothesize, kind: at-rest, scope: 'recorder-'}, carry = counts + finding, no enough (a standing watch), poke at the crossing (while_true False).
decisions.step: unlisted: the at-rest probe that reds the undeclared and the overdue with two distinct identities

decisions.text: No freezegun and no clock library: the clock is frozen by handing fixed timezone-aware datetimes through the now= seam every door carries — DataRecorder.write(now=), stamp_read(now=), probe.census(now)/report(now) and ModuleRaiser.raise_trouble(now=). Isolation is a scratch roots table {repo, commons, instance} -> <tmp>/world (the shape cairn/devices/trouble/proofs/test_trouble.py:490 uses) with recorders at world/devices/<dev>/0/tools/data_recorder/inbound and emissions read back from world/logs/data_recorder/0/*.json. Five teeth: started-on-first-write-never-moves; drain-drains-hold-holds; overdue raises exactly the overdue identity and lands in the log home; inside-frequency raises nothing; undeclared raises no-reader and never overdue. Run bare as PYTHONPATH=. /home/akien/.cairn/venv/bin/python3 cairn/tools/data_recorder/proofs/test_reading_declaration.py.
decisions.step: unlisted: the five-tooth proof on a frozen clock

decisions.text: The WATCHME probe writes NO artifact itself — a probe carries no authority (Law 6). Its trigger takes the population census through the at-rest probe's _recorders(roots) (memoized once per beat under 'recorder_population') and fires the first beat any recorder carries a non-null last_read; carry is the counts as data — recorders, declared, read, read_names, frequencies (the distinct declared set), discriminates (bool), ticket a4c2be029f49, and a one-line finding; enough is read >= 3 AND len(frequencies) >= 2; to='harbor_master', body {nexus: hypothesize, kind: efficacy, ticket}, horizon 2000 beats. The verdict artifact against the WRONG INTENT clause is written by the owner (CC) through cairn.devices.codemother.machines.verdict.verdict.write_verdict from that carried evidence when the poke lands.
decisions.step: unlisted: cairn/tools/data_recorder/probes/declared_cadence_discriminates.py as WATCHME probe with module-level PROBE carrying trigger, carry, enough, and verdict artifact emission

decisions.text: The population census and the discriminates predicate are the two public functions population(*, roots=None) and discriminates(pop) in the WATCHME probe module, so the same numbers the beat carries can be read at rest by hand: PYTHONPATH=. python3 -c 'from cairn.tools.data_recorder.probes.declared_cadence_discriminates import population; print(population())'.
decisions.step: unlisted: declared cadence actually discriminates in the field (WATCHME until measured)

decisions.text: When on_read is None (undeclared) stamp_read behaves as hold: it stamps last_read and clears nothing, returning 0 — only the literal 'drain' drains, because a tool that drained on an undeclared setting would be inventing the default the ticket forbids.

The trigger is exactly: def _trigger(now, context): c = once(context, 'recorder_reading', lambda: report(now)); return bool(c['troubles']). report() does BOTH the raising and the reconcile itself; it constructs ModuleRaiser('data_recorder', roots=roots) inline when no raiser= is handed in (the proof hands none; roots=None means the live tree). A Probe.trigger may call ModuleRaiser.raise_trouble directly — no dispatch, no handler registration; the counting_block:276-285 pattern applies unchanged at the tool rung and the proof's third tooth measures the emission landing under instance/logs/data_recorder/0/.

The at-rest probe's carry is the dict {recorders: int, raised: [identity, ...] sorted, current: [<device>-<instance>-<name>, ...], finding: str}; the undeclared/overdue counts in the finding sentence are derived by identity prefix (recorder-declares-no-reader- / recorder-read-overdue-) from raised, not carried as separate fields. _recorders(roots=None) is the module's population helper — a list of {device, instance, name, dir, reading} for every child dir of every address.held_tool_paths('data_recorder', roots) that carries reading.json or records.jsonl — and census(now, *, roots=None) is the judgement over it; both are module-level functions of reading_is_declared_and_current.py.

The WATCHME probe imports _recorders from cairn.tools.data_recorder.probes.reading_is_declared_and_current and builds population(*, roots=None) over it — {recorders, declared, read, read_names, frequencies}; discriminates(pop) is the enough predicate. It hands NOTHING to the verdict door: the verdict artifact's shape is the door's own (criteria run by instrument, hypotheses dispositioned — cairn/devices/codemother/machines/verdict/verdict.py:write_verdict, an existing tool with its own proofs) and CC writes it from the carried counts when the poke lands; the WATCHME crossing itself is emitted by CC through transitions.emit once the probe module is on disk (the gate resolves ARMED from the ticket's watchme.probe path), not by the probe.
